hints: Focus on bond angle, three atoms in a straight line means the bond angle at the middle atom must be 180 degrees.
Recall the key shapes, tetrahedral is about 109.5 degrees while octahedral has 90 degrees and also 180 degrees between opposite bonds.
Check which molecule has two bonds pointing in exactly opposite directions from the same central atom to give that linear F-X-F or Cl-X-Cl unit.
walkthrough:
**Understand what straight line means**

Think of three atoms A-B-C where B is in the middle. For them to be straight, the angle A-B-C must be 180 degrees.

Bond angle for linear arrangement:
$$\text{angle A-B-C} = 180^{\circ}$$

**Check the organic molecules**

In poly(ethene), $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{-}$, and in propane, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$, every carbon is tetrahedral with four single bonds.

Tetrahedral angle:
$$\text{angle} \approx 109.5^{\circ}$$
So H-C-H, H-C-C and C-C-C are all bent, never 180 degrees.

**Check the inorganic molecules**

Silicon tetrachloride, $\text{SiCl}_4$, is also tetrahedral, so any $\text{Cl-Si-Cl}$ angle is about 109.5 degrees and not straight.

Sulfur hexafluoride, $\text{SF}_6$, is octahedral with six $\text{S-F}$ bonds. Adjacent bonds are 90 degrees apart, but opposite bonds are straight:
$$\text{F-S-F (opposite)} = 180^{\circ}$$

**Make the deduction**

Only the octahedral molecule contains a set of three atoms F-S-F in a straight line. That is the structure you are looking for.

options.A: Incorrect. Poly(ethene) contains only tetrahedral $\text{CH}_2$ groups. All H-C-H and H-C-C angles are about 109.5 degrees, so no three bonded atoms are linear.
options.B: Incorrect. Propane has a C-C-C chain, but each carbon is tetrahedral. The C-C-C angle is about 109.5 degrees, so the three carbons form a bent shape, not a straight line.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{SiCl}_4$ is tetrahedral. Every Cl-Si-Cl angle is about 109.5 degrees, so although it is symmetrical, it has no 180 degree linear unit.
options.D: Correct. $\text{SF}_6$ is octahedral. The four equatorial F atoms and the two axial F atoms give 90 degree angles to neighbours, but any pair of trans F atoms gives F-S-F = 180 degrees, which is three atoms bonded in a straight line.
